claim: A score-based model is a neural network s_theta(x) trained to approximate the score function, the gradient of log-density nabla_x log p(x), via the Fisher-divergence score-matching objective.
quote: s_θ(x) ≈ ∇_x log p(x) ... E_p(x)[‖∇_x log p(x) − s_θ(x)‖²₂]

claim: Song et al.'s ICLR 2021 score-SDE paper introduces a unified framework where a reverse-time SDE removes noise using the perturbed-data score, with a predictor-corrector sampler and the probability flow ODE.
quote: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations

claim: Vincent (2011) proved a denoising-autoencoder training criterion is equivalent to matching the score of an energy model to a Parzen density estimator, giving denoising score matching that avoids second derivatives.
quote: a simple denoising autoencoder training criterion is equivalent to matching the score ... of a nonparametric Parzen density estimator of the data

claim: Tweedie/Miyasawa gives the noise-score identity E[epsilon|Y] = -sigma^2 nabla log p_sigma(Y) and the denoising identity E[X|Y] = Y + sigma^2 nabla log p_sigma(Y), so minimizing the denoising MSE recovers the score.
quote: ∇log p_σ(y) = −𝔼[ε/σ² | Y] ... 𝔼[X|Y] = Y + σ²∇ln p_σ(Y) ... ∇ln p_σ ∈ argmin 𝔼[|f(X+ε)−(−ε/σ²)|²]

claim: For a Gaussian the score is -epsilon/sigma, so DDPM's noise-prediction network is a reparameterized score model: s_theta(x_t,t) = -eps_theta(x_t,t)/sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t).
quote: ∇_x log p(x) = -ε/σ ... s_θ(x_t, t) ≈ ∇_{x_t} log q(x_t) = -ε_θ(x_t, t)/√(1 - ā_t)

claim: Song & Ermon's NCSN estimates scores at multiple noise levels via denoising score matching and samples with annealed Langevin dynamics, the precursor to score-based diffusion.
quote: Noise Conditional Score Networks (NCSN)

claim: Ho et al.'s DDPM (2020) uses an epsilon-prediction parameterization whose simplified objective coincides with denoising score matching over multiple noise scales combined with annealed Langevin-like sampling.
quote: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models

claim: U-Net was introduced by Ronneberger et al. (2015) as a fully convolutional encoder-decoder with a contracting path, an expanding path, and skip connections concatenating encoder features into the decoder for biomedical image segmentation.
quote: The architecture consists of a contracting path to capture context and a symmetric expanding path that enables precise localization.

claim: The U-Net encoder uses two 3x3 convolutions with ReLU followed by 2x max-pooling to downsample, and the symmetric decoder uses up-convolution; skip connections concatenate encoder features into the decoder to preserve spatial information.
quote: The convolutional blocks on the encoder path have two 3x3 convolutional layers, activated with ReLU non-linear function, and followed by a max-pooling operation that reduces the spatial dimension by 2.

claim: Dhariwal & Nichol's ADM ('Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis', 2021) found a better U-Net via ablations, reaching FID 2.97 on ImageNet 128x128, 4.59 on 256x256 and 7.72 on 512x512, matching BigGAN-deep.
quote: We achieve an FID of 2.97 on ImageNet 128×128, 4.59 on ImageNet 256×256, and 7.72 on ImageNet 512×512, and we match BigGAN-deep even with as few as 25 forward passes per sample

claim: ADM's U-Net improvements were: more depth vs width, multi-head attention with 64 channels per head applied at 32x32/16x16/8x8 resolutions, BigGAN residual blocks for up/downsampling, residual connections rescaled by 1/sqrt(2), and adaptive group normalization (AdaGN) to inject timestep and class embeddings.
quote: AdaGN(h,y)=ys GroupNorm(h)+yb ... BigGAN residual block for upsampling and downsampling the activations ... attention at 32×16, and 8 resolutions rather than only at 16×16 ... 64 channels per head

claim: Rombach et al.'s Latent Diffusion Models ('High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models', CVPR 2022 oral) run the U-Net in a compressed VAE latent space and turn the U-Net denoiser into a conditional generator by augmenting it with cross-attention layers over text/other-modality embeddings.
quote: By introducing cross-attention layers into the model architecture, we turn diffusion models into powerful and flexible generators for general conditioning inputs such as text or bounding boxes

claim: In the diffusion U-Net the timestep is represented with sinusoidal positional embeddings (or random Fourier features) and injected into residual blocks via spatial addition or adaptive group normalization; U-Net became the default because of its proven success across computer-vision tasks.
quote: Time representation uses sinusoidal positional embeddings or random Fourier features; these time features are injected into residual blocks via simple spatial addition or adaptive group normalization layers.

claim: The Stable Diffusion U-Net has four stages with channels {320,640,1280,1280}, each with 2-3 ResNet blocks that receive timestep injection, self-attention (8 heads) at coarser resolutions, and cross-attention (8 heads) to CLIP text embeddings; the timestep uses sinusoidal encoding projected by an MLP to 1280 dims.
quote: channels {320, 640, 1280, 1280}, with each stage containing 2-3 ResNet blocks with timestep injection, self-attention (heads=8) for coarser resolutions, and cross-attention (heads=8) to CLIP text embeddings ... sinusoidal encoding with MLP projection to 1280-dim

claim: The CompVis/stable-diffusion reference implementation of the latent text-to-image diffusion U-Net has roughly 72k GitHub stars, reflecting U-Net's dominance as the open-source diffusion backbone.
quote: A latent text-to-image diffusion model

claim: The original CompVis/latent-diffusion repository ('High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models') has about 14k GitHub stars.
quote: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

claim: HuggingFace diffusers packages the conditional U-Net as UNet2DConditionModel; the library has roughly 33.8k GitHub stars and notes the U-Net originates from Ronneberger et al. and is used because it outputs images the same size as the input.
quote: The UNet model was originally introduced by Ronneberger et al. for biomedical image segmentation, but it is also commonly used in Diffusers because it outputs images that are the same size as the input.

claim: DiT (Peebles & Xie) replaces the U-Net with a transformer on latent patches; DiT-XL/2 reaches FID-50K 2.27 on ImageNet 256x256, SOTA at the time.
quote: we initialize the MLP to output the zero-vector for all alpha; this initializes the full DiT block as the identity function

claim: DiT patchifies the 32x32x4 VAE latent into p x p patches giving T=(I/p)^2 tokens; halving p quadruples token count and Gflops, and higher-Gflops DiTs consistently reach lower FID.
quote: We find that DiTs are scalable architectures for diffusion models... DiTs with higher Gflops -- through increased transformer depth/width or increased number of input tokens -- consistently have lower FID.

claim: adaLN-zero regresses scale/shift from the summed timestep+class embedding and zero-inits the residual modulation, beating cross-attention and in-context conditioning while being most compute-efficient.
quote: The adaLN-Zero block yields lower FID than both cross-attention and in-context conditioning while being the most compute-efficient.

claim: Stable Diffusion 3 (Esser et al. 2024, arXiv 2403.03206) builds on DiT with the MMDiT backbone trained under reweighted Rectified Flow.
quote: Stable Diffusion 3 ... reweighted Rectified Flow formulation and MMDiT backbone

claim: MMDiT uses separate weights for image vs text modalities but joins their sequences for a shared attention op; SD3 uses two CLIP encoders plus T5, scaling from 15 blocks/450M params to 38 blocks/8B params without saturation.
quote: separate sets of weights for the two modalities ... joining the sequences of the two modalities for the attention operation ... 15 blocks with 450M parameters to 38 blocks with 8B parameters

claim: FLUX.1 (Black Forest Labs, Aug 2024) is a 12B-parameter rectified-flow transformer using a hybrid of multimodal (MMDiT) and parallel diffusion transformer blocks in the latent space of an image encoder.
quote: All public FLUX.1 models are based on a hybrid architecture of multimodal and parallel diffusion transformer blocks and scaled to 12B parameters.

claim: FLUX conditions on T5-XXL plus CLIP, concatenates text and image tokens for joint attention in MMDiT 'double-stream' blocks, then switches to 'single-stream' parallel blocks; Schnell is a 1-4 step distilled variant.
quote: hybrid architecture of multimodal and parallel diffusion transformer blocks

claim: OpenAI's Sora uses a DiT backbone operating on spacetime patches of video latents that act as transformer tokens, letting it train across variable resolutions, durations and aspect ratios.
quote: Given a compressed input video, we extract a sequence of spacetime patches which act as transformer tokens ... Sora is a diffusion transformer.

claim: PixArt-alpha (Oct 2023) is a DiT-based T2I model that injects text via cross-attention modules added to the DiT block, reaching near-SOTA quality at ~1% of the training cost of RAPHAEL.
quote: incorporating cross-attention modules into Diffusion Transformer (DiT) to inject text conditions and streamline the computation-intensive class-condition branch

claim: Hunyuan-DiT (Tencent, May 2024) is a multi-resolution diffusion transformer with fine-grained Chinese+English understanding, redesigning the transformer, text encoder and positional encoding and adding multi-turn multimodal dialogue.
quote: Hunyuan-DiT, a text-to-image diffusion transformer with fine-grained understanding of both English and Chinese

claim: The official facebookresearch/DiT PyTorch repo has ~8.6k GitHub stars.
quote: GitHub Stars: 8.6k stars ... official PyTorch implementation ... replacing the traditional U-Net architecture with transformers that operate on latent patches.

claim: The official black-forest-labs/flux inference repo has ~25.6k GitHub stars.
quote: GitHub Stars: 25.6k stars ... official inference repository for FLUX.1 models by Black Forest Labs.

claim: Salimans & Ho introduce v-prediction (predicting velocity v) as a stable parametrization for few-step diffusion sampling and distillation.
quote: We present new parameterizations of diffusion models that provide increased stability when using few sampling steps... distill a trained deterministic diffusion sampler... into a new diffusion model that takes half as many sampling steps.

claim: Karras et al. EDM defines a preconditioned denoiser D_theta = c_skip(sigma) x + c_out(sigma) F_theta(c_in(sigma) x; c_noise(sigma)) to standardize input/output scales across noise levels.
quote: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models

claim: EDM preconditioning coefficients: c_skip=sigma_data^2/(sigma^2+sigma_data^2), c_out=sigma*sigma_data/sqrt(sigma_data^2+sigma^2), c_in=1/sqrt(sigma^2+sigma_data^2), c_noise=0.25 ln(sigma), with loss weighting lambda(sigma)=1/c_out^2.
quote: D_θ(x,σ) = c_skip(σ)x + c_out(σ)F_θ(c_in(σ)x; c_noise(σ))... λ(σ) = 1/c_out²(σ) = (σ² + σ_data²) / (σ·σ_data)²... c_skip(σ) = σ_data² / (σ² + σ_data²)

claim: Hang et al. Min-SNR treats diffusion training as multi-task learning and clamps per-timestep loss weights by SNR, giving 3.4x faster convergence and FID 2.06 on ImageNet 256x256.
quote: adapts loss weights of timesteps based on clamped signal-to-noise ratios... 3.4× faster... new record FID score of 2.06 on the ImageNet 256×256 benchmark

claim: Min-SNR-gamma weight is w_t = min(SNR(t), gamma) with SNR(t)=alpha_t^2/sigma_t^2 and default gamma=5; constant weighting suits epsilon-prediction, SNR weighting suits x0-prediction, and v-prediction divides the weight by (SNR+1).
quote: w_t = min{SNR(t), γ}... good performance can usually be achieved when γ is set to 5... when predicting velocity v, the loss weight factor must be divided by (SNR+1).

claim: Liu et al. rectified flow learns an ODE drift v fitting the constant velocity X1-X0 along linear-interpolation paths X_t = t*X1 + (1-t)*X0.
quote: By fitting the drift v with X₁ - X₀, the rectified flow causalizes the paths of linear interpolation Xₜ... Xₜ = tX₁ + (1-t)X₀

claim: DDPM's simplified objective regresses predicted noise to true noise, and the score is s_theta = -epsilon_theta(x_t,t)/sqrt(1-alphabar_t), linking epsilon-prediction to score matching.
quote: L_simple = E[||ε - ε_θ(x_t, t)||²]... s_θ(x_t, t) = -ε_θ(x_t, t)/√(1-ᾱ_t)... minimizing L_ε is equivalent to score matching

claim: v-prediction target is defined as v = alpha_t * epsilon - sigma_t * x0, interpolating between x0- and epsilon-prediction and giving well-behaved targets at all SNR.
quote: v ≡ α_t ε − σ_t x_0

claim: Ho & Salimans' classifier-free guidance jointly trains a conditional and an unconditional diffusion model and combines their score estimates, achieving the quality/diversity trade-off of classifier guidance without any classifier.
quote: guidance can be indeed performed by a pure generative model without such a classifier... we jointly train a conditional and an unconditional diffusion model, and we combine the resulting conditional and unconditional score estimates

claim: In HuggingFace diffusers, the guidance_scale parameter controls how strongly the text prompt influences generation; higher values follow the prompt more closely but too high introduces artifacts.
quote: The `guidance_scale` parameter affects how much the prompt influences image generation... Higher `guidance_scale` values push the model to follow the prompt more closely, and if this value is too high, you may observe some artifacts in the generated image.

claim: Imagen shows generic large frozen language models like T5 are effective text encoders for image synthesis, and scaling the text encoder boosts fidelity and image-text alignment more than scaling the diffusion model itself.
quote: generic large language models (e.g. T5), pretrained on text-only corpora, are surprisingly effective at encoding text for image synthesis... increasing the size of the language model in Imagen boosts both sample fidelity and image-text alignment much more than increasing the size of the image diffusion model

claim: Stable Diffusion 3 Medium is a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT) using three fixed pretrained text encoders (OpenCLIP-ViT/G, CLIP-ViT/L, and T5-xxl) to process prompts before diffusion.
quote: Stable Diffusion 3 Medium is a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT) text-to-image generative model... uses three fixed, pretrained text encoders: OpenCLIP-ViT/G... CLIP-ViT/L... T5-xxl

claim: FLUX.1 Krea [dev], a 12B rectified flow transformer co-developed with Krea AI (July 2025), targets photorealism and avoids the oversaturated 'AI look' of prior text-to-image models.
quote: overcomes the oversaturated 'AI look' to achieve new levels of photorealism

claim: Stable Diffusion 3.5 uses an MMDiT transformer backbone with separate weight sets for image and text representations, adaptive layer norm (adaLN), and adds Query-Key Normalization for training stability.
quote: the integration of Query-Key Normalization into the transformer blocks, which makes the model more stable for training and fine-tuning

claim: Stability AI released the open Stable Diffusion 3.5 family (Large, Large Turbo, Medium) in October 2024, using three text encoders (CLIP-G, CLIP-L, T5-XXL).
quote: Introducing Stable Diffusion 3.5

claim: DiT replaces the U-Net with a ViT-style backbone operating in latent space, capturing long-range dependencies and scaling better; DiT now underpins SD3, FLUX.1, Qwen-Image and SORA.
quote: DiT has become the foundation of many state-of-the-art image generation models, such as Stable Diffusion 3, FLUX.1 and Qwen-Image

claim: Diffusion distillation methods (knowledge, progressive, consistency, score, and adversarial distillation) enable few-step or single-step generation, whereas training-free samplers still require over 10 steps.
quote: Training-based distillation enables few-step or even single-step generation, whereas training-free acceleration via specialized samplers still requires over 10 steps

claim: Latent Consistency Models predict the PF-ODE solution in latent space for 2-4 step sampling (a 768x768 LCM trains in 32 A100 GPU-hours); SDXL-Turbo uses adversarial+score distillation for one step, and SDXL-Lightning uses progressive adversarial distillation.
quote: MLCM distilled from SDXL achieves a CLIP Score of 33.30 with only 4 steps, substantially surpassing 4-step LCM, 8-step SDXL-Lightning, and 8-step HyperSD

claim: Midjourney runs a closed, undisclosed diffusion architecture; it is described not as a conventional model but a service tuned heavily on aesthetic quality, with no published architecture specifications.
quote: it's a service built on a closed diffusion architecture that prioritizes output quality

claim: Ideogram 4.0 (June 2026) is a 9.3B single-stream DiT where text and image tokens are concatenated into one 34-layer transformer sequence, using Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct for text understanding and excelling at in-image text rendering.
quote: single-stream Diffusion Transformer ... Text and image tokens are concatenated into one unified sequence and processed through the same 34-layer transformer

claim: The field is moving toward unified multimodal and autoregressive image generation (GPT Image 1.5, HunyuanImage 3.0, Transfusion, Show-o), with hybrid AR+diffusion transformers blending sequence modeling and diffusion objectives.
quote: Mixed Autoregressive and Diffusion Transformers for Continuous Image Generation

claim: SiT (Ma, Goldstein, Albergo, Boffi, Vanden-Eijnden, Xie, 2024) is built on the DiT backbone but swaps the diffusion formulation for an interpolant framework that connects two distributions more flexibly than standard diffusion.
quote: a family of generative models built on the backbone of Diffusion Transformers (DiT)... the interpolant framework, which allows for connecting two distributions in a more flexible way than standard diffusion based models

claim: The official PyTorch SiT repo (~1.2k stars) ships the model implementation, class-conditional ImageNet-256 pretrained weights, and a DDP training script; the best FID-50K of 2.06 is from the XL/2 model at 256x256.
quote: SiT achieves an FID-50K score of 2.06... Pre-trained class-conditional SiT models trained on ImageNet 256x256... A SiT training script using PyTorch DDP
